definition: The cost of a single ad click.
example: Please compare CPC across creatives.

definition: The cost of showing an ad 1,000 times.
example: This campaign runs on a CPM basis.

definition: The cost of a single valid video view.
example: First check each platform's valid-view criteria.
note: Valid-view duration and qualifying criteria vary by platform and ad product.

definition: A cost paid according to a fixed ad placement duration.
example: We'll run the main screen on a CPT basis for one day.

definition: The ratio of clicks to ad impressions.
example: With 20 clicks and 1,000 impressions, the CTR is 2%.
note: Calculated as clicks ÷ impressions × 100. Distinguish it from metrics that use the number of people as the denominator.

definition: Revenue generated relative to ad spend.
example: We calculate ROAS from ad revenue and cost.
note: A revenue-based metric. It does not directly indicate profit margin or net profit.

definition: The share of visits or clicks that lead to a target action.
example: Signup CVR is the number of signups divided by the number of visits.
note: Check whether the denominator is clicks or visits, and which action is defined as a conversion.

definition: The cost of each target action, such as a purchase or signup.
example: We check the CPA of acquiring one signup.

definition: The total number of times an ad is displayed.
example: If the same person sees it twice, that counts as two impressions.

definition: The number of unique people an ad reached, excluding duplicates.
example: Report impressions and reach separately.

definition: The act of defining who an ad will be shown to.
example: We split targeting by interests.

definition: The people an ad or piece of content is aimed at.
example: Define an audience that matches the campaign goal.

definition: A group of customers divided by shared characteristics.
example: We separate recent buyers into their own segment.

definition: Advertising again to people who had prior contact, such as a visit.
example: We retarget people who visited the cart.

definition: Excluding a specific group from the audience shown an ad.
example: We exclude existing buyers from this campaign.

definition: A unit that records file changes in version history.
example: I committed the login code I edited.

definition: A line of versioning you can work on independently.
example: Start edits on a new branch.

definition: Combining different change histories into one.
example: Once review is done, merge into the main branch.

definition: A proposal to review and incorporate changes.
example: Please describe the reason for the change in the PR.

definition: A separate repository created based on another repository.
example: We fork the open-source repo and make edits.

definition: A space that stores project files and their change history.
example: Docs are managed in the same repository.

definition: An item for recording and tracking bugs, tasks, discussions, and more.
example: Please note the reproduction steps in the issue.

definition: A state where overlapping changes cannot be merged automatically.
example: A conflict occurred because the same line was edited.

definition: Copying a repository and its history to your own computer.
example: First clone the repository locally.

definition: Sending local change history to a remote repository.
example: I pushed the committed work to the remote.

definition: Fetching remote changes and applying them to your current work.
example: Please pull the latest changes before starting.

definition: Creating a new commit that undoes a previous change.
example: I reverted the problematic commit.

definition: An approach that improves a product through short iterations and feedback.
example: We adjust the next tasks based on user feedback.

definition: An agile framework for collaborating with defined roles and iteration cycles.
example: Let's set this sprint's goal together.

definition: A fixed-length work cycle for producing a targeted deliverable.
example: We'll improve search in the next sprint.

definition: A short team meeting to share progress and blockers.
example: In stand-up, start with blocked tasks.

definition: An activity to reflect on past working methods and decide improvements.
example: In the retrospective, pick one thing to change next time.

definition: A unit for estimating the relative size and complexity of work.
example: We set points by comparing with similar tasks.
note: It is not a universal unit that converts directly to time, and it varies by the team's standard.

definition: A collected list of upcoming features, improvements, and fixes.
example: We gather requests in the backlog and prioritize them.

definition: A graph showing how remaining work changes over a period.
example: We check remaining work with the burndown chart.

definition: The processes and activities for ensuring software quality.
example: In QA before release, we check the main user flows.
note: Testing is part of quality assurance. Depending on the team, QA may also refer to a testing phase or the responsible organization.

definition: A test that verifies a small unit of code works as expected.
example: We add a unit test to the price calculation function.

definition: A test that verifies multiple components work correctly together.
example: We integration-test the link between payment and order storage.

definition: The task of separating a desired subject from its background in an image.
example: Please deliver product photos with the background cut out.

definition: Adjusting the spacing between two specific letters.
example: We fine-tune the space between the two letters in the logo with kerning.

definition: Adjusting the spacing across an entire selected range of letters.
example: Please widen the tracking of the body text a little.

definition: The vertical spacing between lines of text.
example: Increase the body leading to make it easier to read.

definition: Visual expression that organizes letterforms, size, spacing, and more.
example: We distinguish headings from body text with typography.

definition: Graphics expressed through the mathematical information of points and lines.
example: Deliver the logo as a vector, which scales well.

definition: An image expressed with a grid of pixels.
example: For raster images, check the original resolution.

definition: A pixel-related measure indicating the level of detail in an image.
example: Check the image resolution against the size you'll use.
note: Pixel dimensions and output density (PPI) should be checked separately.

definition: The number of image pixels placed along one inch.
example: Please check the output size together with the PPI.

definition: A PostScript-based file format used to deliver graphics.
example: We deliver it as the EPS requested by the print shop.

definition: A board that gathers images, colors, and textures to show a creative direction.
example: We share a mood board before producing drafts.

definition: Images or examples referred to when setting a creative direction.
example: Please collect references with the mood you want.

definition: A model or draft that previews how a design will look when applied.
example: We review the packaging design as a mockup.

definition: The process of finishing details such as buttons and hems by hand after sewing.
example: This lot still has the hand-finishing process left.

definition: The side line where the front and back panels of a garment meet.
example: Please check the side-seam stitching.

definition: The finishing work on a garment, including ironing.
example: Please complete the finishing press before shipment.
note: Sources vary slightly, scoping it from ironing-focused work to the entire finishing process.

definition: A sewing worker paid according to work volume or unit price.
example: This process is done on a piece-rate basis.

definition: A term for support staff who assist with other tasks on site.
example: In the records, this term means a person who helps with the work.
note: It can be taken as a demeaning term, so when addressing someone directly we recommend a specific role name such as support staff.

definition: The person in charge of ironing on the sewing floor.
example: We ask the presser to do the final pressing.
note: The source records the ironing worker with this term. 'Ironing' is linked as a search aid.

definition: A sewing technician in charge of overlock work.
example: We assign edge finishing to the overlock operator.

definition: A field term referring to the pattern or ground of a fabric.
example: This fabric has a fairly large pattern.
note: Even with the same Korean spelling, the meaning differs by field. Distinguish the general-work sense of 'fake' from the fashion sense of 'pattern'.

definition: A term for temporary stitching done before the main sewing.
example: Let's set the shape first with basting.

definition: Work that wraps and stitches the edge of fabric.
example: We finish the edge with whipstitching.

definition: The template of shapes and measurements for making each part of a garment.
example: We revise the sleeve pattern based on the sample.

definition: A trial product that confirms form and specs before mass production.
example: We check the sample fit before mass production.

definition: Cutting fabric according to the pattern.
example: We start cutting with the finalized pattern.
note: 'Dachi' is a field term for cutting on the sewing floor.

definition: Stitching cut fabric and other pieces together.
example: We pass cut lots on to sewing.

definition: A term for knit fabric made by circular knitting, or garments made from it.
example: We check the stretch of the circular-knit fabric.
note: The material describes a shirt made from circular-knit fabric. Check the specific material composition separately.

definition: Fabric made by interlacing yarns lengthwise and crosswise, or garments made from it.
example: This shirt is a woven material.

definition: A sewing method for finishing hems or seam allowances on knits and the like.
example: We finish the T-shirt hem with a coverstitch.

definition: A term for sewing work that finishes fabric edges.
example: We finish the scarf edge with overlock edging.
note: This entry is a field term for edge-finishing stitching. Distinguish its context from interlock, which refers to a knit structure or fabric.

definition: The overall outline revealed when a garment is worn.
example: This coat has a relaxed silhouette.

definition: A small sample for checking color, texture, and the like.
example: We attach fabric swatches to the mood board.

definition: A shot composition looking down from a position higher than the subject.
example: I'll shoot the table scene from a high angle.
note: The high angle is organized here alongside the Korean cinematography term. Distinguish it from the top shot, a directly overhead vertical composition.

definition: A shot composition looking up from a position lower than the subject.
example: Please frame the subject from a low angle.
note: Organized as the Korean cinematography term corresponding to the low angle.

definition: A camera composition aligned with the subject's eye level.
example: We shoot interviews at eye level.

definition: A camera composition that tilts the horizon.
example: We convey an uneasy mood with a Dutch angle.

definition: A shot that shows what a character is looking at, as if through their eyes.
example: We add a POV after the shot of the door opening.

definition: A shot that shows the other person over one character's shoulder.
example: I'll continue the conversation scene with an OTS.

definition: Shooting while the camera moves to follow the subject.
example: We follow the walking subject with a tracking shot.

definition: A shot that frames a face or object closely to show detail.
example: Please capture the expression in close-up.

definition: A shot that shows a very small part, such as an eye or hand, large.
example: We shoot just the pupil in extreme close-up.

definition: A shot that frames a subject's upper body to show expression and surroundings together.
example: We'll go with a medium shot for the explanation scene.

definition: A shot that frames the whole figure and surrounding space widely.
example: We need a long shot to show the space.

definition: A shot that frames a wide background and a small subject together from afar.
example: We open the city skyline with an extreme long shot.

definition: A shot looking straight down from directly above the subject.
example: We capture the cooking process with a top shot.

definition: A slang expression for something that is not genuine or has no substance.
example: I was criticized for writing down figures as fakes without actually checking them.
note: Even with the same Korean spelling, the meaning differs by field. Distinguish the general-work sense of 'fake' from the fashion sense of 'pattern'.

definition: An expression for something done or borrowed temporarily.
example: Let's first check whether it was left as a placeholder.
note: An expression confirmed in past language-refinement materials. Its current range of use may vary by site.

definition: An agreed way for programs to exchange functions or data with each other.
example: We receive weather data through the provider's API.

definition: A language that marks up the structure and meaning of web documents.
example: We write the title and body structure in HTML.

definition: A language that specifies the presentation of a web document, such as color, font, and layout.
example: We adjust screen spacing with CSS.

definition: A programming language that implements behavior such as interactivity on the web.
example: We connect button behavior with JavaScript.

definition: A communication protocol for exchanging requests and responses on the web.
example: The browser sends an HTTP request to the server.

definition: A structure that represents a document as a tree of objects so code can manipulate it.
example: We find the title element in the DOM and change its content.

definition: A data-exchange format that expresses keys and values as text.
example: We organize the word data as JSON.

definition: A method of storing data for reuse to speed up the next access.
example: An old cache was showing a previous image.

definition: A reference that points to a particular object.
example: We check whether they are references pointing to the same object.

definition: The height and direction from which the camera views the subject.
example: I'll lower the angle.

definition: A framing of a figure from roughly the chest up to the head.
example: I'll go with a bust shot for the interview.
note: Shot boundaries vary by field convention. Agree specifically on how far down the chest to include.

definition: A framing of a figure from around the waist up to the head.
example: We capture hand gestures with a waist shot.
note: Depending on the document, WS can also stand for Wide Shot. Don't rely on the abbreviation alone—check the framing.

definition: A composition that frames the entire figure from head to toe.
example: Please include the shoes in the full shot.

definition: A composition framing from around the knees up to the head.
example: Show the movement with a knee shot.

definition: A shot centered on a single person.
example: Let's also shoot each person's one shot.

definition: A shot that frames two people together.
example: We start the conversation with a two shot.

definition: A shot that frames several people in one frame.
example: The last one is a group shot.

definition: The basic unit of footage captured in a single composition.
example: We add a reaction after this shot.
note: Shot and its transliterations all render the same English word 'shot'. They are linked to one entry rather than inflated into separate words.

definition: A story unit that generally continues in the same time and place.
example: This scene takes place in a cafe.

definition: A grouping of related scenes that together form a story unit.
example: The chase sequence is over.
note: Here it means a story unit. In editing software it can also refer to a timeline work unit where multiple clips are arranged.

definition: A shot filmed continuously over a long stretch without cutting.
example: We capture from the entrance in one long take.

definition: The empty space between the top of the head and the top of the frame.
example: Reduce the headroom a little.

definition: The empty space placed in the direction of a figure's gaze.
example: Please give eye room on the right.

definition: The empty space in the direction a figure or object is moving.
example: Leave lead room in front of the runner.

definition: A shooting instruction to follow a moving subject within the frame.
example: Follow the actor walking toward us.
note: It refers to the goal of following the subject. You can follow by panning in place or by moving the camera. It differs from the follow focus, a focus-control device.

definition: Each individual attempt at filming the same shot.
example: Let's check with the third take.

definition: The footage selected as usable.
example: This take is the OK take.

definition: Footage kept as a candidate rather than discarded right away.
example: Let's keep this version too.

definition: A shot that separately emphasizes an important object or action in a scene.
example: We need an insert of the hand signing.

definition: Supplementary footage added to the main footage to show context and mood.
example: Please also shoot B-roll of the workshop.

definition: An expression meaning to finish and wrap up the work at hand.
example: Let's wrap today's shoot here.
note: A common expression for finishing work across many job sites. The example for this film entry is written to fit a shooting context. You can replace it with 'end of shoot' or 'wrap-up'.

definition: An expression for finishing and ending the work.
example: Let's wrap this task here.
note: A common expression for finishing work across many job sites. The example for the film entry is written to fit a shooting context. You can replace it with 'end of shoot' or 'wrap-up'.

definition: Turning the camera left or right while keeping its position.
example: Pan toward the entrance.

definition: Turning the camera up or down while keeping its position.
example: Tilt up from the feet to the face.
